title: What If the Arctic Lost All Its Summer Sea Ice?

scenes.text: What if the Arctic lost all its summer sea ice? Models say decades, not centuries.
Since 1978, September sea ice has shrunk by about thirteen percent every decade.
Snow-covered sea ice reflects about eighty-five percent of sunlight. Open water reflects only about seven.
So a blue Arctic would soak up heat the ice used to bounce back to space, speeding up warming.
Climate models put the first ice-free summer somewhere between the years 2032 and 2058, depending on emissions.
The planet's white summer roof would be gone.
